_doc: Trials a SIGNED served-pool notice names that the register must still NOT admit, each with a typed code and the verbatim span that shows why. A notice that names a held trial is excluded WHOLE (its signed 'after' includes the held trial, so no partial application can match it): it is rebuilt without the trial and re-presented. Read by scripts/build_served_pool_additions.py.

holds.span: the stored RR 0.21 is a PER-PROTOCOL analysis of the 63 patients who 'completed the study according to the protocol', not the 87 randomized (46 vs 41)
holds.span_source: outputs/k_gap/g1/probiotics-aad-prevention.json -> Wenus et al72 -> our_refusal (cross-family definition audit)
holds.why: V6-02 enters Wenus with 2/34 vs 8/29 = 63 completers, the per-protocol set; the randomised arms are 46 vs 41. Pooling completers beside randomised denominators is a population mismatch the served pipeline refuses. Found by the captain while building the admission route, after V6 was signed: the derivation's exclusion list checked served-pipeline refusals but not this recorded audit finding.

final.note: the hold is final: notice V6-02 is withdrawn (docs/result_changes.json withdrawal); probiotics stays at V5-01 (k 13)

holds.span: dpp4-mace-t2d 'Hospitalization for heart failure': served k 1, HR 1.00 (0.83 to 1.20) -> no pooled estimate (HARMS_INCOMPLETE: 2 primary-pool trials report it, 1 pooled)
holds.why: V6-01 puts TECOS in the PRIMARY pool. The harms gate then counts TECOS and SAVOR-TIMI 53 as primary-pool trials reporting heart-failure hospitalisation with only TECOS pooled, and suppresses the served HHF estimate. The signed V6-01 notice showed the MACE change only; the HHF withdrawal is a second served change the signer has not seen. Held until both are presented together (next packet).
